summary: Yukei Matsunaga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Koyasan University (~1948–1951), Tohoku University (~1953–1958), and completed his doctorate at Kyushu University in 1977. He held posts at Shuchiin University and Koyasan University.

Yuki Sasaki works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Sasaki held part-time lecturer posts at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, both attested in 2026.
Yuki Takatsukasa specializes in Buddhist studies. Takatsukasa was a doctoral student at Kyoto University (attested 2015) and later served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2017).

Yukihiko Asayama specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Asayama held posts as a professor at Hokkaido University of Education (attested 1986) and as a researcher at South China Normal University (attested 1991).
Yukihiko Matsumura specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Matsumura studied at Tohoku University (attested 2015) and later worked there as a specialist researcher (attested 2026).

Yukihiro Okada works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. Okada studied at the University of Tokyo and under Michael Hahn. Career posts include positions at Kobe Women's University Seto Junior College and adviser at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Yukihisa Yamao was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University from ~1954 to 1963 and later held an academic post there from ~1968 to 2001.
Yukio Hattori was a scholar of Japanology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Nagoya University from ~1951 to 1959 and held a post at Japan Women's University from ~1966 to 1972.
Yukio Kotani is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Hanjiro Tominaga. Kotani served as professor emeritus of comparative literature at Rissho University (attested 2001).

Yukio Sakamoto was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Tohoku University. He was a professor at Toyo University and served as professor, president, and institute director at Rissho University.

Yukio Takeda was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1954–1962). He held posts at Nagoya City University, Hokkaido University, the University of Tokyo (~1977–1995), and Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (~2000–2005).

Yukio Yamanaka specializes in Indology and linguistics. Yamanaka was a graduate student at Kyoto University (attested 1996) and served as a DFG Research Fellow at the University of Göttingen (attested 2015).

Yuko Kamishima specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. After studying at Indiana University, Cambridge, and the University of Tokyo, Kamishima held posts at Waseda University (2006–2016) and became a professor at Ritsumeikan University in 2016.
Yuko Matsuda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. Matsuda studied at Aoyama Gakuin Women's Junior College and held an affiliation at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2001).

Yuko Yokochi is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Groningen. She has served as associate professor at Kyoto University (attested 2002–2022) and on the editorial board of Studies on the History of Śaivism.

Yulian Zeng is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Zeng studied at Fo Guang University, earning a Master of Arts under the supervision of Kirill Solonin, and also studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
Yumi Katayama specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Katayama was a doctoral student at Hiroshima University (attested 2007) and studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 2013).
Yumi Nakamoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Nakamoto held a research post at Ryukoku University in 2012 and was a graduate research student there in 2014.
Yumiko Ishihama is a scholar of Tibetology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Waseda University from ~1980 to 1989 and held an academic post there around 1997.
Yun Ji is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD in Chinese literature from Fudan University in 2006. Ji served as librarian at the Buddhist College of Singapore (attested 2015).
